topic.symptom: A newly built PC does not boot.
topic.title: New Build Won't Boot? Check the CPU Power Cable

script: New build won't boot? Unplug it before opening the case. Check your manual for the CPU power socket. Use your PSU's own CPU cable, not PCIe. Push it all the way in. Plug it back in. Then try booting again.

storyboard.title: New Build Won't Boot? Check the CPU Power Cable
storyboard.narrationStyle: Calm, conversational, one check. The captions are burned into the cut; no voice generated.

beats.visualDirection: A finger presses the stylized PC's power button and rests there; the monitor beside it stays dark. No other symptom is shown.

beats.narration: Unplug it before opening the case.
beats.visualDirection: At the back of the power supply, the power cord comes out of the inlet.

beats.narration: Check your manual for the CPU power socket.
beats.visualDirection: The glass side panel slides off; the camera closes on an empty 8-pin socket in an example layout, outlined amber, marked POSITION VARIES.

beats.narration: Use your PSU's own CPU cable, not PCIe.
beats.visualDirection: Two cable ends face-on: the 4+4-pin end marked CPU, from the PC's own power supply, gets a green tick; the 6+2-pin end marked PCIe gets a red cross.
beats.onScreenText: CPU CABLE FROM YOUR PSU → NOT A PCIe CABLE

beats.narration: Push it all the way in.
beats.visualDirection: Side view: the CPU plug lowers onto the socket, thumbs press it home, its latch hooks over the socket's tab; outlined green.
beats.onScreenText: PUSH IT ALL THE WAY IN → FULLY IN

beats.visualDirection: The camera pulls back from the filled socket; the panel slides back on; at the back, the cord goes back in.
The unlit PC beside the dark monitor, its power button pulsing amber. No one presses it; no boot is shown.

factualGuardrails: Never say: guaranteed cure for boot failures (It may not work; one check, never a guaranteed fix.)
Never say: always the sole culprit behind boot failures (A PC can fail to boot for many reasons; this is one check.)
Never say: identical header placement on all motherboards (Positions vary; the layout is labelled POSITION VARIES and the manual decides.)
Never say: any modular lead swaps freely between different PSU brands (Modular cables can differ between brands, series and models; use the power supply's own cable.)
Never say: successfully boots straight into Windows afterwards (The cut ends before anyone presses the button; no boot is shown or promised.)
persistentDisclosures: Stylized example · not a fix for every PC

claims.proposition: unplug the power cable before working inside the PC
claims.basis: Crucial, "How to Install Memory in Your Desktop" (https://www.crucial.com/support/install-memory-desktop): "Shut down your system. Once your system has been powered off, unplug the power cable." Checked 2026-10-11 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it.

claims.proposition: a missing CPU power cable can stop a PC from booting
claims.basis: ASUS, "[Motherboard] Troubleshooting - No Power/No Boot/No Display (FAQ 1042632)" (https://www.asus.com/us/support/faq/1042632/): "Some motherboard may contain 8-pin EATX12V_1, 4-pin EATX12V_2 and 24-pin EATXPWR, we suggest to connect all three connectors to the power supply." Checked 2026-10-11 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it. Also: ASUS (H87M-PRO user manual, p. 1-24, as quoted on a forum), "H87M-PRO user manual" (https://www.hometheaterforum.com/community/threads/mobo-wont-power-8-pin-cpu-atx-12v.253413/): "Do not forget to connect the 4-pin/8-pin EATX 12V power plug. Otherwise, the system will not boot." Checked 2026-10-11 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it.

claims.proposition: the motherboard manual shows the CPU power connector
claims.basis: ASUS (H87M-PRO user manual, p. 1-24, as quoted on a forum), "H87M-PRO user manual" (https://www.hometheaterforum.com/community/threads/mobo-wont-power-8-pin-cpu-atx-12v.253413/): "Do not forget to connect the 4-pin/8-pin EATX 12V power plug. Otherwise, the system will not boot." Checked 2026-10-11 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it. (the manual documents the EATX12V plug; positions vary by board, so the cut sends viewers to their own manual)

claims.proposition: the cable marked CPU goes to the motherboard's CPU power connector, not a PCIe cable, and the wrong cable can damage components
claims.basis: Corsair, "Can I use a PCI-e cable in the 8-pin motherboard plug?" (https://www.corsair.com/us/en/explorer/diy-builder/power-supply-units/can-i-use-a-pci-e-cable-in-the-8-pin-motherboard-plug/): "The connectors are either labelled as PCIe or CPU. The PCIe cables go to your graphics card, and the cable marked CPU will mount in your motherboards 8-pin header. … The connector is physically different, but also because the cables are wired differently and might damage your components." Checked 2026-10-11 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it.

claims.proposition: use the CPU cable supplied with that power supply, since modular cables can differ between models
claims.basis: Seasonic, "Which cables are compatible with my Power Supply? (Knowledge Base 68)" (https://knowledge.seasonic.com/article/68-cable-compatibility): "Cables are often not compatible between brands, and even within a brand, modular cables may differ between series and models. Seasonic recommends using the DC cables supplied with the power supply." Checked 2026-10-11 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it.

claims.proposition: push the connector until it is fully in place
claims.basis: Corsair, "PSU: How to Avoid Current Overload/Connector Issues" (https://help.corsair.com/hc/en-us/articles/10700487373197-PSU-How-to-Avoid-Current-Overload-Connector-Issues): "Make sure connectors click fully into place." Checked 2026-10-11 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it.
